what: A single character image (img or inline SVG) is put into WebGL as a 48×40 grid mesh, and each bone (axis → tip, radius r) swings its limb by ± an angle on a 1.6s cycle of (0.5 − 0.5cos). The weight switches on from 30–50px before the bone and switches off r to r+30px away from the shaft, so arms bend out from the torso. The eyes close for 140–220ms every 2–6 seconds (35% of the time they blink once more after 250–450ms), and the shader fills the eye area with the surrounding color and draws a horizontal line. If a shadow slot is given, the same shape is offset by (−168, 128) and painted in the text color, laid down with a 6px blur and .4 opacity.

options.w: Artwork coordinate width — bone and eye coordinates are based on this width, the default artwork’s original width (viewBox for SVG)
options.h: Drawing coordinate height, original height of the default drawing
options.shadow-x: Shadow horizontal offset (image coordinates px), default -168

from.where: feature.html .feature-intro__chara — original FeatureCharaMesh (4 bones · 1600ms · 48×40 · eye radius 14 · shadow −168/128 · blur 6)

note: Bones go in data-bones and eyes in data-eyes as JSON (original character values if absent). Inline SVG bakes in the colors computed at attach time — if you change the skin, reattach the parts. The original keeps separate body and shadow drawings, but the parts make the shadow from a single body
